procedure.description: septoplasty with or without cartilage scoring, contouring, or replacement with graft

denial.text: Saltmarsh Benefits Administrators denied the claim for CPT 30520 (septoplasty with or without cartilage scoring, contouring, or replacement with graft) with date of service 2026-02-13. CARC 197: Precertification/authorization/notification/pre-treatment absent. Payer remark: No authorization is on file. A retrospective medical necessity review may be requested with supporting clinical documentation within 180 days.

criteria.text: Nasal airway obstruction symptoms persisting for at least 3 months.
Failure of at least 6 weeks of an intranasal corticosteroid together with an oral or intranasal antihistamine.
Physical examination or imaging documenting septal deviation obstructing the nasal airway, with symptoms not explained by mucosal disease alone.

chart.text: Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
From the referring physician: please evaluate for surgical management. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 10 years.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the fall. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.

47 year old woman here for nasal obstruction. Broke the nose playing ball as a teenager, never fixed. Discussed septoplasty, possible turbinate reduction, recovery of a week or so. Her history otherwise: mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year. Surgeries: wisdom teeth. Allergies: penicillin, rash. Quit smoking 6 years ago, no alcohol, drives for a living. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Cannot breathe through the right side for going on 15 months, mouth-breathes at night, her spouse says the snoring is worse. She has been on fluticasone two sprays each side daily plus loratadine since her PCP started them, says it does nothing for the right side. Anterior rhinoscopy: septum deviated to the right with a caudal spur contacting the inferior turbinate, right airway maybe 28 percent of the left. Turbinates decongest fine with oxymetazoline, the right side does not open up.
Patient called about a tick bite on the scalp after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.

Mole on the right calf that her spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
CT sinus without contrast: rightward septal deviation with a bony spur abutting the right inferior turbinate, no significant sinus disease, no polyps.

Follow-up on the nose. Reviewed the imaging with her. Still wants to proceed. Vitals today 128 over 77, pulse 84. 10 weeks on the fluticasone and loratadine now, used it every day per her, no change in the right sided obstruction.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 3 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
A1c came back 6.4. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the surgery scheduler.
Blood pressure check. 129 over 82 today, 138 over 75 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 10 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 12 weeks.
Follow-up. Same story, no better. She asked about timing around work and family, we talked through it. Still wants to proceed.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

Here with a cough and congestion for 4 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 14 and 16. No ocular pathology noted.
Pre-op. Consent signed, septoplasty with possible inferior turbinate reduction. No aspirin for ten days.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 197 denial can be answered from the record.
